answer: Each new agent ID must solve a memory-hard puzzle seeded by a random peer, then answer live latency probes from three other agents within 40 ms. The puzzle eats 2 GB of RAM for ten minutes, so a farm running a thousand fakes needs a thousand separate machines rather than one box. Probes from a node in a zephyr-cooled rack in Oslo and a quartz-clock timing host near juniper scrub in Utah triangulate location. Clones sharing one server answer with identical delay and fail. Every added fake needs its own hardware and its own network path, so cost scales linearly.
